annotations.text:
REDESIGNED AS A LEARNED SOCIETY PUBLISHES, not as a product landing page.

Gone, because they were what made the last draft read as marketing: the centred value proposition with paired buttons, the floating image collage, the statistics band, the icon trio of "pillars", the member testimonial, and the closing call-to-action banner.

In their place, the conventions of the genre: a news-led lead story with a sidebar of briefs, a kicker and a date on every item, hairline rules instead of shadowed cards, square corners, a densely populated navigation that is itself the value, and information rather than persuasion — membership categories with their dues, the four steps of admission, the committee by office, and the published documents with their version numbers.

royalsociety.org and istructe.org are both blocked by this network's policy, so this is the genre worked from first principles. Neither society's design is reproduced.

TYPE — one decision needs your approval. Newsreader, a serif, now carries the editorial headlines; Public Sans carries interface and reading copy; Quicksand is held back for the logo lockup alone.

The guideline's rounded geometric is a friendly face, and at headline size it reads promotional. A serif is what gives an institution its register. This is a proposed extension to the guideline, not a departure from the identity — the logo is untouched.

Colour is unchanged and now structural rather than decorative: maroon for the utility strip, section rules, kickers and primary actions; the darkened green only on links.

The eight photographs are still generated placeholders, now desaturated so they read as photographs rather than brand-coloured panels. Each is badged. See the README for what to send.
